title: Weather Alert — Beyond the 956: Tropical Storm In-fa Tracked East of Guam; No Threat Expected, Island at Normal Readiness
excerpt: Tropical Storm In-fa is spinning in the open Pacific about 1,465 miles east of Guam with 40 mph winds — and forecasters say it is no threat to the island. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center's track keeps its closest pass more than 1,000 miles away next Thursday, the National Weather Service in Guam has posted no watch or warning, and Guam remains at Condition of Readiness 4, its normal readiness level, as the island finishes recovering from Super Typhoon Champi.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

WEATHER ALERT — Friday, October 23, 2026 (Saturday, October 24 in Guam)

A new tropical storm named In-fa has formed in the open western Pacific and is being tracked east of Guam — but forecasters say it is no threat to the island. The National Weather Service in Guam has issued no tropical storm or typhoon watch or warning for Guam, and the island remains at Condition of Readiness 4 (COR 4), its normal readiness level, according to the Guam News Network's "Guam Right Now" island conditions page, refreshed Saturday morning, October 24, Chamorro Standard Time.

Where In-fa is now. As of the latest reports out of Guam, Tropical Storm In-fa was centered about 1,465 miles east of Guam, moving southeast at just 1 mph, with maximum sustained winds of 40 mph and gusts to 52 mph, according to the Guam News Network conditions page, which draws on Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) and National Weather Service Guam data. The JTWC, which designates the system 30W (In-fa), placed it near 10.6 degrees north latitude and 166.3 degrees east longitude in its Warning #2 — deep in the open Pacific, north of the Marshall Islands and far from any populated island in the Marianas chain.

The forecast keeps it far away. On the JTWC forecast track, In-fa is expected to strengthen over open water and curve through the remote Pacific, making its closest pass to Guam around 4 a.m. Thursday, October 29 (ChST) — still about 1,039 miles to the east of the island, by then as a typhoon with winds of about 138 mph. In other words, even at its closest and strongest, the storm is forecast to pass more than a thousand miles from Guam. The National Weather Service in Guam's latest advisory, issued Saturday, October 24, at 7:58 a.m. ChST, carries no tropical storm or typhoon watch or warning for Guam.

One more disturbance on the board. Forecasters are also monitoring a second disturbance, Invest 97W, about 1,428 miles east of Guam. The JTWC rates its chance of developing into a tropical cyclone within 24 hours as low, according to its October 24, 2026, 7:00 a.m. ChST assessment reported on the Guam News Network conditions page.

Guam stays at normal readiness. Guam's Condition of Readiness 4 — the island's normal, day-to-day readiness posture — was declared in a Guam Homeland Security / Office of Civil Defense (GHS/OCD) release on October 18, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. ChST, and it remains in place. Nothing in the current outlook calls for that to change.

Still finishing the Champi cleanup. The monitoring comes as Guam wraps up its recovery from Super Typhoon Champi, which passed about 10 miles south of the island on October 18. The Guam Power Authority reported on October 22 that the island's power system had reached 99% of its normal load — a recovery In-fa is not expected to interrupt.

Webb Watch 956 will keep tracking JTWC advisories on In-fa and Invest 97W and will update this story if the forecast changes.

Sources: Guam News Network, "Guam Right Now" island conditions page (refreshed October 24, 2026, 10:48 a.m. ChST); Joint Typhoon Warning Center (assessment of October 24, 2026, 7:00 a.m. ChST; Warning #2 for Tropical Storm 30W (In-fa)); National Weather Service Guam (advisory of October 24, 2026, 7:58 a.m. ChST); Guam Homeland Security / Office of Civil Defense (GHS/OCD); Guam Power Authority.
